standard.title: Openwell Submersible Pumpsets — Specification (First Revision) (खुले कुएँ के लिए निमज्जनी पंपसेट — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the manufacturing requirements, material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and performance testing protocols for openwell submersible pumpsets (both monoblock and coupled types) designed to operate completely submerged in water in open wells, sumps, or reservoirs.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the manufacturing requirements, material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and performance testing protocols for openwell submersible pumpsets (both monoblock and coupled types) designed to operate completely submerged in water in open wells, sumps, or reservoirs.

version.current_version: First Revision, 2018 (Reaffirmed 2022) incorporating active Amendment No. 1 (June 2024)

certification.description: Mandatory Certification under national Quality Control Orders (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Every openwell submersible pumpset sold or distributed in India must carry the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped on its nameplate to certify safety and energy-efficiency compliance.
requirements: Any numerical value representing the final observed or calculated result of an efficiency percentage, specific speed, flow rate, or dimension must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The motor must be a wet type, operating completely filled with clean water, utilizing high-grade copper winding wire insulated with water-resistant thermoplastic (PVC or XLPE) to prevent dynamic winding-to-casing shorts.
The shaft must be made of high-tensile stainless steel to prevent galvanic corrosion and lockups during prolonged submersion.
The pumpset must be fitted with ample-sized, double-sealed ball bearings or water-lubricated thrust pads designed for zero-maintenance operation in grit-containing water.

Under Amendment No. 1 (June 2024), standard efficiency curves are replaced with equations adopted from Commission Regulation (EU) No. 547/2012 to enforce minimum eco-design efficiency index (MEI) limits.

For single-stage end-suction volute pumps, minimum pump efficiency is calculated as: ȠP = 88.59*x + 13.46*y - 11.48*(x^2) - 0.85*(y^2) - 0.38*x*y - 133.82, where x = ln(ns), y = ln(Q), and Q is flow in m³/h.
For multistage diffuser pumps, minimum pump efficiency is calculated as: ȠP = 0.6571*ns + 0.0851*Q - 0.00534*(ns^2) - 0.000565*(Q^2) + 0.00106*ns*Q + 42.
Calculated multistage efficiency must be multiplied by 0.98 for 2-stage pumps and by 0.97 for single-stage diffuser pumps.
To calculate minimum overall pumpset efficiency, the minimum pump efficiency is multiplied directly by the motor efficiency factor.
Assembled motors must pass an under-water leakage current test at rated voltage to verify that the wet winding insulation prevents any electric shock path into the well water.
